focus: Q3 only (other iterations cover Q1, Q2, Q4 and Q5 concurrently, so stay on Q3): check .skilled/commands/doctor/update.md and doctor-update-presentation.txt against the sk-create-command contract in .skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-command/ (thin router, presentation split, argument-hint, allowed-tools, approval gates, dry-run, rollback) and against the three doctor-update-*.yaml workflows. Report every contract violation and every place the router, presentation and workflows disagree, with file:line evidence.
answeredQuestions: Q3: Do update.md and doctor-update-presentation.txt meet the sk-create-command contract (thin router, presentation split, approval gates, dry-run, rollback), and do they agree with the workflows?

label: Apply maps cancellation and interruption to STATUS=DECLINED in the presentation (.skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-update-presentation.txt:212), and its workflow has no cancelled terminal status (.skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-update-apply.yaml:197-203). The sk-create-command contract requires STATUS=CANCELLED ACTION=cancelled when the user aborts (.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-command/SKILL.md:367-381). Since the doctor command contract marks update apply as a gated mutating operation (.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-command/assets/command-contract.json:241-244), cancellation is currently indistinguishable from an explicit refusal. Add the required cancellation status and action to the presentation and state schema.

The apply workflow's top-level pass policy says dry_run_writes_nothing is true (.skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-update-apply.yaml:31-35), but its state-log phase requires a log on every terminal path including dry-run (.skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-update-apply.yaml:191-195). The presentation also prints the state-log path in the apply result (.skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-update-presentation.txt:320) while saying dry-run stops after the plan (.skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-update-presentation.txt:212). Clarify that dry-run skips release-managed writes but still writes an audit log, or remove the dry-run log write.

The router's argument-hint includes --include-prerelease and is 139 characters (.skilled/commands/doctor/update.md:3), within the sk-create-command 140-character limit (.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-command/SKILL.md:214-219). The canonical doctor argument_hint omits --include-prerelease (.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-command/assets/command-contract.json:200-203), although it is an accepted router/workflow input. The frontmatter and machine-readable family contract therefore drift. Synchronize the contract hint with the shipped router.

The router grants Grep and Glob alongside Read and Bash (.skilled/commands/doctor/update.md:4), but neither Grep nor Glob appears as a tool call in the router or its three workflows. The sk-create-command contract says to list only tools actually used and not add broad tools just in case (.skilled/skills/sk-doc/sk-create-command/SKILL.md:217-220). Remove the two unexplained grants or document their required use.

The router calls bare /doctor:update a read-only check (.skilled/commands/doctor/update.md:16), while the check workflow permits git fetch writes to the object store and FETCH_HEAD when release objects are missing (.skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-update-check.yaml:17-24, 61-69). The router summary narrows this to no checkout-file changes (.skilled/commands/doctor/update.md:64), but the presentation only lists --offline and does not disclose the network/Git-metadata exception (.skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-update-presentation.txt:23-31). Qualify the read-only wording and surface the fetch exception so operators can distinguish working-tree safety from a fully offline/no-metadata-write check.
